body.statement:
There are fixed numerical constants \(C_{\mathrm{fixed}},c_{\mathrm{risk}}>0\) with the following property.  For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and every positive variance-bound constant \(C_\epsilon\) in the uniform-intensity exact-witness interface, there is a concentration threshold \(c_{\epsilon,C_\epsilon}>0\).  For every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and every recipe carrying that exact witness at intensities \(u=C_{\mathrm{fixed}}n\) and \(v=C_{\mathrm{fixed}}(n+m)\), let \(\Delta\) be its actual raw-center separation.  If that recipe's raw mixture laws have total variation at most \(1/8\) and \(kBa\le c_{\epsilon,C_\epsilon}\Delta^2\), then
\[
 R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_{\mathrm{risk}}\Delta^2.
\]
This implication holds for every qualifying exact-witness recipe, including both the exact \(b_\epsilon L/(u+v)\) specialization and the C55 bandwidth supplied through the uniform-intensity inequality; the transfer does not select a recipe.  It preserves the identical random \(P_{XA}\) law and holds for the fixed, unequal sample sizes.
body.proof_tex:
Fix the sufficiently large numerical intensity multiplier \(C_{\mathrm{fixed}}\) and the numerical risk multiplier \(c_{\mathrm{risk}}\) once and for all.  Now fix \(\epsilon\), a positive witness variance bound \(C_\epsilon\), and an arbitrary recipe carrying the uniform-intensity exact-witness interface and satisfying the displayed premises.  Let \(S\) and \(T_j\) be its raw total mass and raw target, and let \(\Delta=|ET_1-ET_0|\).  The normalized target is \(\tau_j=T_j/S\).  Since \(0\le T_j/S\le1\),
\[
 |\tau_j-ET_j|\le|T_j-ET_j|+|S-1|.                                \tag{C51}
\]
Chebyshev's inequality and the variance bound imply (after choosing \(c_{\epsilon,C_\epsilon}>0\) sufficiently small as a function only of \(\epsilon\) and \(C_\epsilon\)) that \(kBa\le c_{\epsilon,C_\epsilon}\Delta^2\) gives
\[
 \Pi_j\{|\tau_j-ET_j|>\Delta/4\}\le1/16.                          \tag{C52}
\]
The two center intervals in (C52) are disjoint.  Thresholding any estimator halfway between the centers and charging either a target-concentration failure or squared loss at least \(\Delta^2/16\) shows that, when the two raw mixture laws have total variation at most \(1/8\), their raw-experiment Bayes squared risk is at least \(c_0\Delta^2\) for a numerical \(c_0>0\).

We transfer this conclusion to fixed samples.  If \(\Delta^2\le c_1/n\), the label-gated parametric floor \(\mathrm{lem:parametric\mbox{-}label\mbox{-}floor}\) gives \(R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c/n\ge(c/c_1)\Delta^2\), so suppose \(\Delta^2>c_1/n\).  Use the already fixed multiplier and take raw intensities \(u=C_{\mathrm{fixed}}n\) and \(v=C_{\mathrm{fixed}}(n+m)\).  Conditional on the raw masses, the labeled total is \(K_L\sim\operatorname{Poi}(uS)\); conditional on \(K_L\), its ordered records are iid from the normalized law.  Independently, the auxiliary total is \(K_U\sim\operatorname{Poi}(vS)\), and its ordered records are iid from the normalized \(P_{XA}\) law.

On \(S\ge3/4\), Poisson lower-tail bounds give
\[
 P(K_L<n)+P(K_U<m)\le e^{-c_2C_{\mathrm{fixed}}n}+e^{-c_2C_{\mathrm{fixed}}(n+m)}.                   \tag{C53}
\]
On \(S<3/4\), (C47) and Chebyshev give \(P(S<3/4)\le16kBa\).  Choose the epsilon/variance-bound-dependent threshold \(c_{\epsilon,C_\epsilon}\) so that, with the already fixed \(C_{\mathrm{fixed}}\), (C53), using \(\Delta^2>c_1/n\), and the mass failure together have probability at most \(c_0\Delta^2/8\).

Given any fixed-sample estimator clipped to \([-1,1]\), apply it to the first \(n\) and \(m\) ordered records on the success event and output zero otherwise.  The conditional success experiment is exactly \(P^{\otimes n}\otimes P_{XA}^{\otimes m}\).  Since loss is at most four, its raw Bayes risk is at most the fixed-sample worst-case risk plus \(c_0\Delta^2/2\).  Comparison with the raw lower bound and then infimization over fixed-sample estimators proves \(R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_{\mathrm{risk}}\Delta^2\).  The recipe was arbitrary and the normalized priors are unchanged throughout, so the implication holds for every qualifying exact-witness recipe and equality of their full random \(P_{XA}\) law is preserved.
